### LOW: Installer now persists a Host\-header\-derived coordinator URL into provider\.toml
[coordinator/api/install\.sh:324](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/082a3c349624dfa67667124238614c95d286fe08/coordinator/api/install.sh#L324) · A-008, T-040, TB-002

The new bind\_provider\_coordinator\(\) writes whatever COORD\_URL the served installer carries into \[coordinator\] url in \~/\.config/darkbloom/provider\.toml\. Any non\-production https://host\[:port\] value passes the host regex\. T\-040 already notes that installer and enrollment URLs fall back to the request Host and X\-Forwarded\-Proto headers when baseURL is unset\. If an unset baseURL or a cache or proxy in front of the coordinator lets an attacker influence that value, a victim running \`curl \| bash\` gets more than a one\-time bundle fetch from the attacker host\. The attacker host is persisted as the provider's coordinator, so every later \`darkbloom login\` and \`start\` sends the provider's login and API tokens \(A\-008\) and its attestation and App Attest evidence \(A\-010, A\-015\) to it, and the provider serves traffic for it\. Bundle hash and Developer ID signature checks still limit code substitution, but the persistent rebind of the trust target is new\. Impact depends on how production sets baseURL, which this PR does not show\. Fix: do not write a non\-production URL unless the installer was fetched from a configured, allowlisted base URL\. Alternatively require an explicit opt\-in flag or env var for non\-production binding, and print a clear confirmation of the target host\. The coordinator should also stop deriving the substituted URL from the Host header\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Installer now persists the serving coordinator URL into provider\.toml, widening Host\-header\-injection impact
[coordinator/api/install\.sh:278](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/082a3c349624dfa67667124238614c95d286fe08/coordinator/api/install.sh#L278) · A-008, T-040, TB-002

bind\_provider\_coordinator \(install\.sh, line \~278\) writes the COORD\_URL baked into the served installer into \[coordinator\] url in provider\.toml for any coordinator other than the production URL\. The host regex accepts any https host\. When the coordinator has no baseURL set, the installer URL is derived from the request Host header \(see the 'derives from request host when baseURL unset' test, T\-040\)\. A poisoned or cached installer response, or a spoofed Host, would then give an attacker host a persistent provider registration endpoint\. That endpoint would receive the provider's login and API token and its attestation material on every later \`darkbloom start\`\. Before this change, the effect was limited to the install\-time download\. The bundle hash and Developer ID signature checks still protect the binary\. Fix: require baseURL to be configured in production, or restrict the bound host to an allowlist\. Also document the persistence in the T\-040 mitigations\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5
